historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Benzothiazepine calcium-channel blockers

starting.description: A Tanabe CNS-oriented synthetic benzothiazepine program, itself informed by known psychotropic precedents, yielded a coronary vasodilating effect during broad biological screening. The investigators then developed the observed cardiovascular activity through related compounds and structure-activity studies, leading to diltiazem.

inspiration.description: Observed coronary vasodilation by synthesized benzothiazepines redirected a CNS-oriented program; prior psychotropic compound effects were an antecedent to that series. No natural molecular isolate is asserted.

steps.description: Thiazesim and a benzodiazepine hydroxyl-substitution precedent informed a new synthetic series intended for central nervous system activity. A contemporary synthesis paper cites the earlier antidepressant benzothiazepine work.
A broad screen found coronary vasodilation, prompting structure-activity studies and selection of diltiazem.
In anesthetized dogs, researchers compared structural substitutions and stereoisomers; the d-cis acetoxy derivative CRD-401 was the most potent among those tested.
In subsequent investigations of the vasodilator mechanism, the investigators reported a calcium-antagonist property.

design.description: The team synthesized a new 3-hydroxy benzothiazepine series, pursued structural variation after observing coronary effects, and compared cis/trans and optical isomers. The d-cis acetoxy derivative showed the strongest activity of their tested series, while the acetoxy analogue lasted longer than the hydroxy comparator in the reported dog experiment; a stereoselective route provided a key synthesis intermediate.

circumstances.description: Synthesis for CNS activity and the broad screening program were deliberate; the account does not explicitly establish whether the coronary effect was personally unexpected.

limits: This record concerns the benzothiazepine calcium-channel blocker class represented by diltiazem, not the independently arising dihydropyridine or phenylalkylamine families.
The source-specific program relates to the founding diltiazem lineage; later benzothiazepines are not separately traced and should not automatically inherit every development detail.
A synthetic lead and its later stereochemical optimization do not by themselves distinguish discovery from scratch from observation-led research.
conflicts: Godfraind 2017 (E7) groups Tanabe with coronary-dilator programs, which can suggest a cardiovascular aim from the outset. The Tanabe investigators' more detailed 1988 account (E1-E2) describes a preceding CNS-oriented synthesis and a screen-to-coronary transition. The overview may be describing the subsequent cardiovascular stage, but neither source explicitly reconciles the framing.
gaps: Sato et al. 1971 was located by PMID 5171789 but no abstract or full text was read; its details cannot be independently asserted.
The original screen notebook, exact first active structure and its contemporaneous CNS-to-coronary transition record were not located. The specific sequence rests on the investigator retrospective.

The original Krapcho thiazesim and Bell oxazepam reports, earlier 1970 Tanabe synthesis articles and clinical-development studies were not read. The Japanese retrospective was interpreted from relevant sections with a working translation, not a certified human translation.
